blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand-hygiene adherence monitoring and feedback
stem: A hospital audits hand-hygiene opportunities and completed actions, then reports the results to staff. What is the primary purpose?

options.A: Use the findings mainly to compare individual staff performance for annual review, with unit discussion focused on personnel below target.
options.B: Use the audit scores as a substitute for further education after initial training because repeated measurement demonstrates staff competence.
options.C: Use the findings to identify adherence gaps and provide prompt, regular feedback to personnel and leadership so infection-prevention practice can improve.
options.D: Use the data to document compliance trends for reporting while leaving any practice changes to each unit's discretion after the audit cycle.

rationale: C is correct. CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that facilities should identify and monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices and provide prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes to healthcare personnel and facility leadership. Surveillance data should also be acted on to improve practice. A overemphasizes individual performance management rather than system improvement. B incorrectly treats measurement as a substitute for education and training. D disconnects collected data from the feedback and improvement actions CDC expects.
educational_objective: Use infection-prevention audit data to identify adherence gaps, provide prompt and regular feedback, and support corrective improvement rather than treating measurement as an end in itself.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC Core Practices page current and rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Core Practices Table, Category 4 Performance Monitoring and Feedback: identify and monitor adherence; provide prompt, regular feedback to healthcare personnel and facility leadership; use standardized monitoring; act on surveillance data. Category 2 Education and Training: provide job-specific training and additional training for recognized lapses. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and promote staff/workplace safety.
source_claim_supported: CDC directly supports monitoring adherence, providing prompt regular feedback, and acting on collected data; monitoring does not replace education or exist merely for reporting or discipline.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and promote staff/workplace safety.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed p.8 was screenshot-verified on 2026-08-21 and visibly includes infection-prevention principles and staff/workplace safety.

option_audit.A: Plausible management use of audit data but incorrect as the primary infection-prevention purpose because CDC emphasizes adherence monitoring plus feedback and improvement rather than punitive ranking.
option_audit.B: Plausible measurement-focused shortcut but incorrect because CDC separately requires education/training and additional training for recognized lapses.
option_audit.C: Correct; directly matches CDC performance-monitoring and feedback requirements.
option_audit.D: Plausible reporting function but incorrect because CDC expects feedback and action on collected data rather than passive reporting.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths are reasonably balanced: A 138, B 141, C 154, D 140 characters; the key is only modestly longer and not structurally more detailed than the distractors.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified: A narrows the purpose to performance review, B replaces required education, and D omits feedback/action; C uniquely matches CDC's stated performance-monitoring purpose.
